Use Tier 2: add candidate-conditioned history attention to the existing SASRec network. The latest trial reached 0.4975 macro HR@10 versus the 0.5050 baseline, with Electronics falling from 0.42 to 0.36 despite gains in Movies_and_TV and CDs_and_Vinyl. These results motivate testing whether compressing every history into one final-position vector loses interests relevant to individual candidates.

Focus on model_design and training_evaluation. For each candidate, use its item embedding as a query over the causally encoded history states, mask padding, and pool the relevant states. Fuse this pooled representation with the existing final-position representation through a learned projection before computing one neural ranking score. Train the attention and fusion parameters jointly with the backbone using the existing sampled-softmax objective; each supervised transition must attend only to its available prefix. Keep the remaining architecture, sampling, optimizer, and training settings unchanged to isolate this architectural addition.

Train one independent model per category with seed 42, retain the supplied splits and preprocessing, and select one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the modified network and use exactly the same scoring path as validation, preserving all four dataset routes. Compare macro and per-category HR@10 under the pinned host evaluation, retaining DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and all artifacts beneath the trial directory. This tests whether candidate-specific retrieval of earlier interests improves ranking without introducing independently fitted predictors or accessing hidden test data.
